theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is the main benefit of a paraffin wax treatment on the hands?
options: It removes unwanted hair from the backs of the hands
It softens and moisturises the skin and warms the joints
It hardens the nails so that they never break again
It lightens the dark patches of skin found on the knuckles

questions.stem: How does paraffin wax help the skin to take in moisture?
options: It dissolves the top layer of dead skin away
It cools the skin down and closes up the pores
It bleaches the skin so that it is lighter
It traps heat and seals in moisture and cream

questions.stem: Which client is likely to gain the most from a paraffin wax treatment, once her doctor agrees?
options: A client with stiff, aching finger joints from arthritis
A client with a fresh, painful burn on the back of her hand
A client with a fungal infection between the toes
A client who has lost all feeling in her fingers

questions.stem: Which condition stops a paraffin wax treatment on the hands?
options: Dry skin on the knuckles
Short, bitten nails
Open cuts on the fingers
Rough skin on the palms

questions.stem: Why is loss of feeling (numbness) in the hands or feet a contraindication to paraffin wax?
options: The wax will not stick to skin that has no feeling
Numb skin makes the wax set far too slowly to peel off later
She may not feel that the wax is too hot, and so be burned

questions.stem: A client has a verruca (a wart on the foot). What should you do about a paraffin foot treatment?
options: Dip the foot for longer so that the heat kills the verruca
Cover the verruca with nail polish and then dip the foot
Carry on as normal; a verruca cannot spread to others

questions.stem: A client has diabetes. What is the right action before a paraffin wax treatment?
options: Check with her doctor first, and take extra care with heat
Use the wax hotter than normal, since she feels less
Dip her feet straight away, because the heat helps her blood sugar

questions.stem: What should be checked on the hands and feet during the consultation before paraffin wax?
options: The colour of her nail polish and her ring size
Cuts, rashes, infections, swelling and loss of feeling
How long she has been letting her nails grow out this year

questions.stem: How should the paraffin wax be tested before the client's hand goes in?
options: Ask the client to put one finger in quickly to feel it
Test it on your inner wrist, then on a small patch of her skin
Look at the wax; if it is clear and runny it is safe

options: Wet skin makes the wax turn a yellow colour in the bath
Water makes the wax set too hard to peel off later
Wet hands will make the wax in the bath smell bad
Water with hot wax can cause burns and spoils the wax

questions.stem: When a hand is dipped into the paraffin bath, what must the client avoid?
options: Touching the bottom or sides of the bath
Spreading her fingers slightly apart as she dips
Keeping her hand quite still in the wax
Breathing slowly and staying relaxed

questions.stem: Why is paraffin wax never heated in a pot on a gas stove in the salon?
options: The wax would turn into a liquid that cannot set
The stove would make the wax smell of the food cooked there
Without a thermostat it can overheat and catch fire
The flame would make the wax far too cool to use

questions.stem: What should you do if paraffin wax is spilled on the floor?
options: Mop it up at once with hot water
Let it cool and set, then scrape and peel it up
Sweep it under the couch where it is out of the way of clients
Pour more wax on it to soften it

questions.stem: What does the thermostat on a paraffin bath do?
options: It keeps the wax at a steady set temperature
It filters the dirt out of the used wax
It times how long the client's hand is wrapped
It shows how much wax is left in the bath

questions.stem: Why should the lid be kept on the paraffin bath when it is not in use?
options: To stop the clients in the salon from smelling the wax
To stop the wax from turning into a gas
To make the wax darker and thicker
To keep dust and dirt out and hold in the heat

questions.stem: Why are the client's hands cleaned with an antibacterial product before dipping?
options: To make the wax stick more strongly to the skin
To soften the cuticles so they can be pushed back later
So germs are not carried into the shared wax bath
To cool the hands so the wax feels less hot

options: Melt it again in the bath for the next client
Throw it away; never put it back in the bath
Keep it in a bag for the same client next week
Rinse it in water and put it back in the bath

questions.stem: Which way of applying paraffin wax is the most hygienic for each client?
options: Dipping every client's hands into the same bath without cleaning them
Letting the client dip her own hands as often as she likes
Painting the wax on with a brush that is used for all clients

As many times as she wants

questions.stem: Why should the client keep her hand still after it has been dipped?

A plastic liner, then a towel or thermal mitt
Kitchen foil, pressed tightly round the wrist
Nothing; it is left uncovered to set

questions.stem: About how long is paraffin wax usually left on the wrapped hands before it is removed?
options: About 10 to 15 minutes
About 1 to 2 minutes
About two hours or more
Until the next morning

questions.stem: How is paraffin wax removed from the hand?
options: Wash it off the hand under a hot tap
Scrape it off the skin with a sharp metal nail file
Peel it off from the wrist towards the fingers
Leave it on to fall away by itself later

questions.stem: In a manicure, why is paraffin wax applied before the nail polish, not after?
options: The heat of the wax would make the polish dry much faster and harder
The wax leaves oil on the nails that must be cleaned off first
Polish must always be the very first step of a manicure
Paraffin wax would turn the polish a darker colour

questions.stem: Which method can be used to apply paraffin to an area, such as an elbow, that cannot be dipped?
options: Pour the wax straight from the bath onto the skin
Ask the client to lean over and rest her arm in the bath

Brush the warm wax on in layers with a clean brush

questions.stem: Why is a hand cream or treatment lotion often applied before the paraffin wax?
options: The warm wax helps the cream to soak into the skin
The cream stops the wax from feeling warm on the skin at all
The cream makes the wax set into a hard shell
The cream cools the bath down to a safer heat

questions.stem: What extra check should you make before a paraffin wax treatment on the feet?
options: That the client has painted her toenails red
That the client is wearing open-toed shoes
Check for athlete's foot, verrucae and cuts
That the client has walked to the salon that day

questions.stem: After paraffin wax, a client's skin is slightly pink and warm. What does this usually mean?
options: She has a burn and must go to hospital at once
It is a normal sign of more blood flowing to the skin
She is allergic to wax and cannot have it again
The wax was too cold and must be made hotter

questions.stem: A client says the wax is burning just after her hand is dipped. What should you do?
options: Tell her to keep it on for a while, as the feeling will soon pass
Wrap the hand more tightly to keep the heat in
Dip the hand again to add a cooling layer
Remove the wax at once and cool the skin with cool water

questions.stem: A small burn appears after paraffin wax. Which first aid is correct?
options: Cool it under cool running water and record what happened
Cover it with a little more wax to protect it from the air
Rub hand cream into it firmly straight away
Prick any blister that forms so that the fluid can come out

questions.stem: Paraffin wax can catch fire. Which rule follows from this?
options: Keep the bath next to a window in direct sunlight
Store the spare blocks of wax on top of the warm heater
Keep it away from naked flames and do not overheat it
Light a candle beside the bath to show it is on

questions.stem: Before switching on the paraffin bath, what should you check?
options: That the plug and cable are not damaged
That the wax is mixed with a little water
That the bath is full to the very brim
That the room lights are switched off

questions.stem: When should the paraffin bath usually be switched on before a treatment?
options: Just as the client sits down at the station
The night before, and left on all night unattended
Only once the rest of the treatment has finished
In time for the wax to melt fully, as the maker says

questions.stem: How should a paraffin bath be cleaned and kept in good order?
options: Never clean it, because the hot wax keeps it clean
Clean it and change the wax as often as the maker's instructions say
Fill it with water and boil it dry each evening
Wash it out with bleach while it is still switched on

questions.stem: Which aftercare advice should you give after a paraffin hand treatment?
options: Wash the hands in very hot water to remove the oils
Do housework without gloves to toughen the skin
Use hand cream daily and wear gloves for housework
Rub the hands with lime juice to keep them soft

questions.stem: Why should a client protect her hands from the sun after a hand treatment?
options: Sun makes the nails grow too fast
Sun can dry, darken and age the skin
Sun turns the paraffin back into a liquid
Sun stops the cuticles from growing

questions.stem: Why are the temperature test and the client's reaction written on the record card?
options: So the client can be charged for the test
So the wax can be sold at a higher price
So that the record card looks complete
So the next therapist can treat her safely

questions.stem: Where is the best place to put the paraffin bath during a manicure?
options: On a stable surface where it cannot be knocked
On the floor beside the client's chair, near her feet
On the client's lap, so she can reach it easily
On a high shelf, so that no one can reach it

questions.stem: Why is some paraffin wax sold with added oils for beauty use?
options: To make it get hotter and last for longer in the bath
To turn it into a hair removal wax
To make it safe to use on cuts and broken skin
To make it more moisturising and pleasant to use

questions.stem: A client is allergic to perfumes. Which paraffin wax should you choose?
options: One with the strongest scent you have
A plain wax with no added perfume
Any wax, as long as she cannot smell it
A wax with lime oil to calm the skin

questions.stem: In a pedicure, when is a paraffin foot treatment usually given?
options: Before the feet have been cleaned or soaked at all
After the toenail polish has been painted on and has dried
After the feet are clean and dry, before the polish
While the feet are still wet from the soak

questions.stem: A client, Mrs Samuels, has dry, rough hands from washing clothes by hand. How will a paraffin treatment help?
options: It softens the skin and helps it hold moisture
It removes the need to wear gloves for washing
It makes the skin waterproof for several weeks
It stops the hands from sweating in the heat

questions.stem: A client's hands become itchy and blotchy after paraffin with a scented lotion. What is the most likely cause?
options: The wax was not hot enough
She kept her hand too still
An allergy to the lotion or scent
The towel was wrapped too loosely

questions.stem: How should paraffin be applied to the feet if the bath is too small to dip them safely?
options: Ask the client to stand in the bath for a minute
Brush it on, or use a liner with a portion of wax
Skip the wax and apply ice to the feet instead
Pour the hot wax from a height onto the soles of the feet

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

essays.stem: Explain what a paraffin wax treatment is, how it works on the skin, and which clients benefit most from it.
essays.modelAnswer: Paraffin wax is a soft wax made from petroleum, often with added oils. It is melted in a paraffin bath with a thermostat and kept at the working temperature the maker gives. The hands or feet are covered in several thin layers. As the wax cools, it sets into a warm, close-fitting coat. This coat holds the heat in and seals the skin, so that moisture and any cream underneath cannot escape. The warmth increases the blood flow, softens hard skin and cuticles, and helps the skin take in the cream. It also eases stiff, aching joints and feels relaxing. Clients who benefit most are those with dry, rough or cracked skin, for example from washing clothes by hand, cleaning or gardening, and those with stiff joints from arthritis, once their doctor agrees. It also suits clients who simply want a soothing extra treatment with a manicure or pedicure.
markingPoints: Describes paraffin wax and the heated bath with a thermostat
Explains that it sets into a coat that holds heat and seals in moisture
Benefits: softens and moisturises skin, increases blood flow
Benefits: eases stiff joints and is relaxing
Names clients who benefit (dry, rough skin; stiff joints with a doctor's approval)

essays.stem: Describe the consultation you would carry out before a paraffin wax treatment, including the contraindications you would look for.
essays.modelAnswer: I explain the treatment and complete the record card with the client. I ask about her health: diabetes, poor circulation, heart or blood pressure problems, any loss of feeling in her hands or feet, recent injuries or operations, and allergies to creams, perfumes or wax. I look closely at her hands or feet in good light. Open cuts, burns, sunburn, broken or inflamed skin, rashes, and infections such as athlete's foot, fungal nails, verrucae or warts mean I do not carry out the treatment, and I advise her to see a doctor or pharmacist. Swelling or a recent injury also stops the treatment. Loss of feeling and poor circulation are a risk because she may not feel if the wax is too hot. Diabetes and heart conditions need her doctor's approval first. If she is allergic to perfume, I use an unscented wax and cream. I agree the treatment and price, and the client signs the card.
markingPoints: Asks about health (diabetes, circulation, loss of feeling, heart), injuries and allergies
Examines the hands or feet in good light
Names conditions that stop the treatment (cuts, burns, infections, rashes, swelling)
Explains the risk of loss of feeling; gets a doctor's approval where needed
Adapts products for allergies; agrees the plan and has the card signed

essays.stem: Describe how you would prepare the paraffin bath and the work area, and how you would make sure the wax is a safe temperature.
essays.modelAnswer: I place the paraffin bath on a stable, heat-proof surface where it cannot be knocked, near a socket, with the cable tidy and away from water. I check the plug and cable for damage before switching it on. I switch it on early enough for the wax to melt fully, as the maker says, and set the thermostat. I keep the lid on while it heats and never leave it on unattended. I lay out disposable liners, thermal mitts or towels, a clean brush, hand cream, antibacterial gel, a lined bin and the record card. When the wax has melted, I check its temperature with the thermometer if the bath has one. Then I test a little wax on my own inner wrist. If it feels comfortable, I test a small area of the client's skin and ask her how it feels before I go on. If it is too hot, I turn the thermostat down and wait.
markingPoints: Bath on a stable surface, cable tidy and checked, away from water
Switched on in good time, thermostat set, lid on, never left unattended
Work area laid out with liners, mitts, cream, gel and bin
Checks the temperature, then tests on the therapist's inner wrist
Tests on a small area of the client's skin and asks her before going on

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how you would give a paraffin wax treatment to a client's hands using the dip method.
essays.modelAnswer: After the consultation, I wash my hands and clean the client's hands with an antibacterial product. I check that her hands are completely dry and that she has removed her rings and watch. I apply a treatment cream or lotion if one is used. I test the wax on my inner wrist, then on a small area of her skin. I ask her to spread her fingers slightly and dip one hand into the wax up to the wrist, without touching the bottom or sides, then lift it out and hold it still for a few seconds. She dips again, usually about three to five times in all, as the maker says, each time a little lower than the last so the edge stays even. I cover the hand with a plastic liner and then a thermal mitt or towel, and repeat for the other hand. After about 10 to 15 minutes I remove the mitts and peel the wax off from the wrist towards the fingers. I throw it away and massage in any cream that is left.
markingPoints: Cleans the client's hands, checks they are dry and removes jewellery
Tests the wax on the inner wrist, then on the client
Dips with fingers slightly apart, not touching the bottom or sides, holding still between dips
Several dips (about three to five), then wraps in a liner and mitt or towel
Leaves for about 10 to 15 minutes, peels from wrist to fingers and throws the wax away

essays.stem: Explain how you would keep a paraffin wax treatment hygienic, and why the wax must never be put back in the bath.
essays.modelAnswer: A paraffin bath is shared by many clients, so it must be kept free of germs. I wash my hands before and after each client. I clean the client's hands or feet with an antibacterial product before any wax is applied, and I never treat skin that is broken or infected. Where possible I use the portion method: I take out the wax a client needs into a disposable liner or bowl, or brush it on with a clean brush, so that her skin never touches the main bath. Wax that has been on a client's skin is never put back into the bath, because it carries dead skin, sweat and germs that would pass to the next client. It goes in a lined, lidded bin. I use a new plastic liner for each client and clean the thermal mitts as the maker says. I keep the lid on the bath, and I clean the bath and change the wax as often as the maker advises.
markingPoints: Hand washing and cleaning the client's skin before treatment
Never treats broken or infected skin
Uses the portion or brush method so the client does not touch the main bath
Used wax never put back, with the reason; disposed of in a lined bin
New liners for each client; mitts and bath cleaned and wax changed as the maker says

essays.stem: Describe how you would carry out a paraffin wax treatment on a client's feet, including the extra checks and the method you would use.
essays.modelAnswer: Feet need extra checks because infections are common there. I look between and under the toes and on the soles for athlete's foot, verrucae, fungal nails, corns, cracks and cuts. If I find an infection or broken skin, I do not apply the wax and I suggest she sees a doctor, pharmacist or podiatrist. I clean and dry the feet well, often after a foot soak and scrub in a pedicure. I apply a foot cream. I test the wax on my inner wrist and then on a small area of her foot. Because feet are large and the bath is shared, I usually brush the wax on in several even layers, or pour a portion of wax into a disposable foot liner and place the foot in it, moving the wax over the skin. I wrap each foot in a plastic liner and then a thermal bootie or towel, and raise the feet so she is comfortable. After about 10 to 15 minutes I remove the wax from the ankle downwards and throw it away.
markingPoints: Checks for infections, cracks and cuts on and between the toes; refers if found
Cleans and dries the feet and applies cream
Tests the wax on the inner wrist, then on the client
Uses a hygienic method (brush or portion in a liner) in even layers
Wraps, leaves for about 10 to 15 minutes, removes and throws the wax away

essays.stem: Describe the contra-actions that can happen during or after a paraffin wax treatment, and what you would do for each.
essays.modelAnswer: Slight pinkness and warmth are normal, because the heat increases blood flow, and they soon fade. A burn can happen if the wax is too hot, if the skin is wet, or if the client cannot feel heat well. If she says the wax is burning, I remove it at once and cool the skin under cool running water. I do not put cream, butter or ice on a burn, and I do not burst blisters. I get first aid help if needed. An allergic reaction, such as itching, a rash or blotches, may be caused by the wax, the cream or the perfume in them. I stop, remove the product, rinse with cool water and advise her to see a doctor if it does not settle. If the client feels faint or unwell, I stop the treatment and let her rest with some water. I write any contra-action on her record card and report it to my supervisor, and I check the thermostat before the next client.
markingPoints: Normal pinkness and warmth explained
Burn: remove the wax and cool under cool running water; no creams, ice or bursting blisters
Allergic reaction: stop, remove, rinse and refer if needed
Feeling faint or unwell: stop and let her rest
Records and reports the contra-action and checks the equipment

essays.stem: Explain how you would use, look after and clean a paraffin bath safely, including fire and electrical safety.
essays.modelAnswer: Paraffin wax can catch fire if it is overheated, so it is only heated in a proper paraffin bath with a thermostat, never in a pot on a stove or near a flame. I place the bath on a stable surface, away from water, with the cable tidy so no one trips or pulls it. I check the plug and cable before use and report any damage instead of using it. I fill it only to the line the maker shows. I keep the lid on and never leave it switched on and unattended or overnight. Hands and tools must be dry before they go near the wax. If wax spills, I warn others, let it cool and set, then scrape and peel it up so no one slips. At the end of the day I switch it off and unplug it. I clean the outside with a suitable cleaner when it is cool, and I change the wax and clean the inside as often as the maker says.
markingPoints: Heated only in a bath with a thermostat, never on a stove or near a flame
Stable placement, tidy cable, checked plug and cable; faults reported
Lid on, filled to the line, never left on unattended
Spills cooled and peeled up; others warned
Switched off and unplugged; cleaned and wax changed as the maker says

essays.stem: Explain where a paraffin wax treatment fits into a manicure and a pedicure, and why it is placed there.
essays.modelAnswer: In a manicure, the nails are first cleaned of old polish, filed and shaped, and the cuticles are softened and tidied. The hands must then be clean and completely dry before the paraffin, so that the wax does not trap dirt or water. A hand cream or lotion is applied, and the paraffin is put on over it so that the heat helps it to soak in. After the wax is removed, the rest of the cream is massaged in, or the hand massage is given. The paraffin always comes before the polish. The wax and cream leave oil on the nails, so the nail plates are wiped with remover before the base coat; otherwise the polish will not stick. In a pedicure the order is the same: soak, clean, nail and hard-skin work, then dry the feet, apply cream and paraffin, then massage, cleaning the nails and polish last. A client who wants only paraffin can have it on its own, after cleaning.
markingPoints: Comes after nail shaping and cuticle work, on clean, dry skin
Cream or lotion applied first so the heat helps it soak in
Comes before the polish, with the reason
Nails wiped free of oil before the base coat
Correct order given for a pedicure as well

essays.stem: Describe the aftercare advice you would give after a paraffin wax treatment, and what you would write on the record card.
essays.modelAnswer: After the treatment the skin is soft, warm and moisturised. To keep it that way, the client should apply a hand or foot cream every day, especially after washing, and wear gloves for housework, washing clothes and gardening. She should protect her hands from strong sun with a sunscreen, because Jamaica's sun can dry and darken the skin. She should avoid very hot water for the rest of the day. For feet, she should dry well between the toes and wear clean, well-fitting shoes. If any redness, itching or soreness appears, she should contact the salon, and see a doctor if it does not settle. I suggest how often to return, for example every few weeks with her manicure or pedicure. On the record card I write the date, the areas treated, the method used, the products, the result of the temperature test, how she reacted, the advice I gave and any products she bought. I sign it and keep it private.
markingPoints: Daily cream and gloves for housework
Sun protection and avoiding very hot water
Foot care advice and reporting any reaction
Advises when to return
Records date, area, method, products, temperature test, reaction and advice

practical1.title: Paraffin wax hand treatment using the dip method
practical1.brief: Work in pairs in the Centre's salon and take turns as therapist and client. In a group of five, one member works on a model who has agreed to take part. Each member holds a consultation, checks her client's hands for contraindications and completes the record card. She cleans the client's hands with an antibacterial product, applies a hand cream, tests the wax on her own inner wrist and then on the client's skin, and gives a paraffin wax treatment to both hands by the dip method. She wraps the hands, times the treatment, removes the wax correctly, throws it away and massages in the remaining cream. Each member also takes one job for the group: setting up and checking the paraffin bath with the assessor, laying out the station, taking the photos, or the final clean-up. Photograph each stage below. Photos show the hands and the work area only. Hand in once for the whole group, with the record cards.
materials: Paraffin bath with a thermostat (and a thermometer if available), filled with paraffin wax
Antibacterial hand gel or wipes, and hand cream
Disposable plastic liners, thermal mitts or towels
A lined, lidded bin and salon disinfectant
photos: The paraffin bath set up on a stable surface with a tidy cable, and the station laid out
The wax being tested on the therapist's inner wrist
The client's clean, dry hands with cream applied
One hand after the dips, showing an even layer of wax
The hands wrapped in liners and mitts
The wax being peeled off from the wrist towards the fingers
The station cleaned, with the used wax in the bin
checklist: Held a consultation, checked the hands for contraindications and completed the record card
Checked the bath, plug and cable and set the thermostat as the maker says
Cleaned the client's hands and made sure they were dry, with jewellery removed
Tested the wax on the inner wrist, then on the client, before dipping
Guided the client to dip correctly without touching the bottom or sides
Wrapped and timed the treatment correctly
Removed the wax from wrist to fingers and threw it away, never back into the bath
Gave aftercare advice and left the station clean and safe
safety: Test the wax on your inner wrist, then on the client, before every treatment
Do not treat broken, infected or numb skin
Keep hands, tools and the area around the bath dry
Never leave the bath switched on and unattended; keep the lid on when not in use
If the client feels burning, remove the wax at once, cool with cool running water and tell the assessor

practical2.title: Paraffin wax foot treatment using the brush or liner method
practical2.brief: Work in pairs in the Centre's salon and take turns as therapist and client; in a group of five, one member works on a model who has agreed. Each member holds a consultation and checks her client's feet carefully, including between the toes, for infections, cracks and cuts. Anyone with a contraindication is not treated, and her partner works on a model instead. Each member cleans and dries the feet, applies a foot cream, tests the wax, and applies paraffin to both feet by brushing on even layers or by using a portion of wax in a disposable liner. She wraps the feet, raises them for comfort, times the treatment, removes and throws away the wax, and finishes with a short foot massage to work in the cream. She writes the aftercare advice on a card for the client. Each member also takes one job for the group: setting up the bath, preparing the foot basins, taking the photos, or cleaning and disinfecting at the end. Photograph each stage below, showing the feet and the work area only. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Paraffin bath with a thermostat, filled with paraffin wax
Foot basins, foot cleanser or antibacterial wipes, and towels
Clean wax brushes and disposable foot liners
Couch or pedicure chair with a footrest
Salon disinfectant, gloves and a lined, lidded bin
photos: The feet being checked between the toes at the consultation
The clean, dry feet with cream applied
The wax being tested on the therapist's inner wrist
Paraffin brushed on or in a liner, showing even layers
The feet wrapped in liners and booties or towels
The finished feet after the wax is removed and the cream massaged in
Basins and station cleaned and disinfected
checklist: Checked the feet, including between the toes, and acted correctly on any contraindication
